blocks.text: Current source P approves room C; Q lists C capacity 10. Draft says room C is approved, seats 10 and offers lunch.
Approval and capacity are supported by P and Q; lunch lacks evidence. A grounded answer reports the first two claims and does not invent lunch.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Source A approves room H; B lists H capacity 7, except maintenance limit 4. Maintenance status is unknown. Write a grounded response.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Room H approval is supported. State the conditional capacities 7 normally and 4 during maintenance, with status unresolved; do not choose an unconditional capacity.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Grounding requires support for the exact claim, including conditions; attaching a source name is insufficient.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

rows: Query terms red sensor. D1 text red sensor manual; D2 text red paint. Their lexical scores are 2 and 1. Vector query [1, 0], D1=[.4, .9], D2=[.8, .1].

For a toy lexical score, count distinct query terms present after lowercase exact-word matching. For a toy vector score use a stated dot product. Compare relevance using independent judgments, not score magnitude alone.
Lexical ranks D1 first; dot product ranks D2 first (.8 versus .4). The supplied task relevance favours the sensor manual; vector ranking alone does not prove relevance.
